title: Isandro and the Promise
premise: Marine biologist Oscar Kavanagh, still raw from a betrayal that ended her engagement and her research funding, hires a stranger named Isandro Reyes to pose as her boyfriend at her family's reunion on the coast. What begins as armor becomes real: Isandro, it turns out, is the estranged heir to the development company threatening to pave over her turtle sanctuary, and he took the job to see the land his father wants destroyed. As their fake romance deepens into something neither can deny, Oscar must confront the guilt she carries from choosing survival over principle years ago, while Isandro must decide whether inheriting power means repeating his father's corruption or breaking it. At the climax, Isandro publicly opposes his family's board vote, risking everything, and Oscar must forgive herself before she can accept that second chances arrived exactly on time. They end together, rebuilding the sanctuary as partners.
about_author: Juniper Amberdale is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who wrote her first romance on the back of sea turtle nesting surveys. She lives near the water and believes every love story deserves a second hatching.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. On the sanctuary beach at dawn, Oscar counts a failed nest and dodges a call from her ex-fiancé, establishing her habit of measuring life in data instead of feelings. Her sister texts: bring someone to the reunion or face questions alone. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A boat charter leaves her stranded, and Isandro Reyes, quiet, watchful, offers a ride. Their banter crackles; he seems oddly familiar with the coastline. She impulsively asks if he'd like to be paid to attend a family reunion. Emotional beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over bad coffee they negotiate the fake-dating contract: no real feelings, one weekend, cash up front. Isandro hesitates at the sanctuary's name but signs anyway. Emotional beat: the thrill of a deal that feels like a dare.

chapters.title: Arrival at Kavanagh House
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The reunion begins: her mother's appraisal, her ex-fiancé Marcus smug among the guests, her sister's knowing looks. Isandro plays his role too well, charming everyone including Oscar. Emotional beat: performance becoming comfort.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During dessert, Isandro defends Oscar against Marcus's barbs with a conviction that surprises himself. Under the table, their hands touch and neither pulls away. He recognizes the sanctuary land from his father's blueprints. Emotional beat: the fake date turning fatally real.

chapters.title: The Morning After the Lie
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The reunion ends; the contract should too. Instead Isandro lingers, helping rescue stranded hatchlings at midnight. Oscar catches him photographing the property line and feels the first cold drop of doubt. Emotional beat: suspicion blooming inside warmth.

chapters.title: What Isandro Knows
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Flashback chapter: Isandro is heir to Meridian Development, sent by his dying father to secure the coastal parcel. He took Oscar's offer to see the land before deciding its fate. Now he can't separate the woman from the deal. Emotional beat: divided loyalty.

chapters.title: Second Date, First Truth
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Isandro asks Oscar out properly, no contract. She says yes but keeps him at arm's length, revealing only fragments of how Marcus's betrayal cost her funding and reputation. Emotional beat: intimacy offered in installments.

chapters.title: The Board Meets
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Via video call, Meridian's board votes to fast-track the resort. Isandro stalls, citing environmental review, buying the sanctuary time. His father accuses him of weakness. Emotional beat: the first open rebellion.

chapters.title: Nesting Season
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Weeks pass in stolen weekends: tagging turtles, sharing histories. Oscar admits she once stayed silent about a colleague's falsified data to save her own career, the sin she's never forgiven. Emotional beat: confession as trust.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar finds Isandro's folder: surveys, blueprints, the Meridian logo. She confronts him; he confesses who he is but swears he came to stop the project. Shattered, she orders him off her beach. Emotional beat: betrayal echoing the old wound.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With Oscar gone silent, Isandro returns to the city and faces his father directly, refusing to sign. His father threatens to disinherit him and push the vote through without him. Emotional beat: the price of principle made concrete.

chapters.title: The Mirror
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Alone, Oscar realizes she cast Isandro as Marcus because forgiving him would mean forgiving herself. Her sister forces the reckoning: you survived by compromising once; don't let survival become your identity. Emotional beat: turning inward.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar visits her old mentor and finally apologizes for the silence that ended his career. He forgives her, gently, which hurts more than anger. She understands forgiveness isn't earned, it's chosen. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The board reconvenes. Isandro stands before them and reveals the sanctuary's ecological findings, publicly opposing the resort and his father. He's voted out of the company he was born to inherit. Emotional beat: sacrifice completed.

chapters.title: News Travels
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar learns through a journalist that Isandro torched his inheritance to save her sanctuary, and that his father is now dying and demanding reconciliation. She drives through the night to find him. Emotional beat: urgency of unfinished love.

chapters.title: The Hospital Corridor
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Outside his father's hospital room, Oscar and Isandro reunite. He doesn't ask her to stay; she chooses to. Inside, Isandro's father, bitter and diminished, shows what power hoarded becomes. Emotional beat: compassion for the unforgivable.

chapters.title: Climax: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The county hearing on the coastal parcel arrives early, forced by Meridian's remaining executives. Oscar testifies with her data and her whole history, including her past compromise, owning it publicly. Isandro speaks last, renouncing his claim. Emotional beat: both standing exposed and unafraid.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The county grants the sanctuary permanent protection. In the empty hallway after, Isandro tells Oscar he has nothing left to offer but himself. She answers that it's the only thing she ever wanted. Emotional beat: full-circle joy.

chapters.title: Hatching
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Nesting season peaks; hundreds of hatchlings make the sea. Oscar and Isandro walk the beach together, no contract between them, her hand in his by choice. Emotional beat: quiet wonder.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro proposes not with a ring but with a deed amendment naming Oscar co-steward of the land. She laughs, cries, and says yes before he finishes. Emotional beat: love as shared stewardship.

chapters.title: Second Chances
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epilogue. One year later: the sanctuary thrives, Isandro teaches coastal ecology, and Oscar counts turtles and heartbeats now, both plentiful. Closing line mirrors the opening dawn. Emotional beat: peace earned, timing forgiven.
